messages:
elaine: Heads-up — spotted an odd routing case in staging: projectless API keys are getting attributed to the org default project which is blowing past the org quota. Anyone seen this before?

matt: hmm, saw a signal yesterday in the quota dashboard but assumed it was a metric spike. can you paste the request headers/route? :eyes:

elaine: minimal repro — request uses header `Authorization: ApiKey proj:null:abcd1234` (we emit proj:null when users delete a project but keep keys). Route logs show: `auth.lookup -> org-default-bind` then `quota.apply(org)`

sanjay: interesting — our authz middleware currently falls back to org when project claim is missing. previously done to avoid hard rejects. that behaviour predates quota v2.

kim: Oof. That fallback was intended for legacy keys, but quota semantics changed. It should probably map to a special "projectless" bucket instead of org.

rachel: +1. If we attribute to org we risk double counting and billing noise. Also a safety issue if org has tight SLOs.

matt: quick patch idea: on missing project claim, set attribution to `org:<org-id>-projectless` and apply projectless quotas (defaults to zero). That keeps org metrics clean.

elaine: will that break any console UX? some dashboards show per-project breakdown, might show an extra phantom project.

kim: small UX hit but preferable. we can label it "Unattributed (deleted project)" and hide in default UI unless advanced filter.

sanjay: telemetry note: we should emit a new tag `auth.attribution=fallback:projectless` so we can run queries and ensure this isn't getting abused. also include `auth.key_state=deleted-project`

matt: agree. also add a sampling metric for request body size & prompt hash so we can check for forged keys.

elaine: implementation plan: 1) auth-service change to set projectless bucket + tags 2) quota-service change to recognize projectless quotas (defaults 0) 3) console label + hide. Can someone own 1? I can PR 2 and 3.

kim: I can pick up auth-service change. will target a small flag `AUTH_PROJECTLESS_TO_ORG=false` and flip after we validate.

rachel: I'll update telemetry docs and add the new tags to the logging schema. Also add an alert: if projectless count > 0.5% of total keys in org for 1h, page eng-platform.

matt: ops-bot triggered canary deploy yesterday on auth-service — @ops-bot any rollout notes?

ops-bot: deploy 2024-04-28T17:40:22Z auth-service v2.13.1 -> canary hosts (3/20). No errors detected in health checks. Rolling metrics: auth.lookup latency +0.8ms, errors unchanged.

elaine: thanks. kim, when can you cut the PR?

kim: aiming EOD. will add unit tests + small e2e. if all green, deploy to staging and we can run synthetic requests with deleted-project keys.

sanjay: once in staging, let's run a quick A/B: leave fallback-to-org on a subset, and compare quota and billing attribution delta.

rachel: tagging PMs — this affects billing accuracy. @jon-pm FYI.

elaine: cool. want to avoid a panic in prod, so plan: keep old behaviour behind flag, flip after 48h of staging with <0.02% difference.

matt: sounds safe. also add a dashboard panel for `auth.attribution=fallback:projectless` over time + per-org spikes.

elaine: thanks all — will make the tickets and link PRs here. we can reconvene after staging run. :thumbsup:
